title: Describing a pet's symptoms at the vet
objectives: Describe what your pet has been doing
Ask the vet if the other pet needs an examination

courseTemplate.setting: Mila has been scratching her left ear. The owner noticed dark wax. There is another cat at home. Practise communication, with any care decisions left to the vet.

roles.learner: A pet owner accompanying a cat
roles.partner: A vet asking for information and explaining follow-up

courseTemplate.openingLine: What seems to be the problem with Mila today?

targetPatterns.pattern: She's been scratching her left ear constantly.

stages.title: Describe what your pet has been doing
stages.instruction: Use the course facts to invite this task. A natural prompt is “What seems to be the problem with Mila today?”
successCriteria: The learner can describe what your pet has been doing in their own words.
hints: You can start with “She's been scratching her …”

stages.title: Describe an additional observation
stages.instruction: Use the course facts to invite this task. A natural prompt is “Have you noticed any discharge, smell or wax?”
successCriteria: The learner can describe an additional observation in their own words.
hints: You can start with “I've noticed a little …”

stages.title: Ask the vet if the other pet needs an examination
stages.instruction: Use the course facts to invite this task. A natural prompt is “Thanks. I'll examine Mila's ear and explain the next steps.”
successCriteria: The learner can ask the vet if the other pet needs an examination in their own words.
hints: You can start with “We have another cat …”

Have you noticed any discharge, smell or wax?
